decisive_items: cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas
well-circumscribed, 11.8 cm cystic mass in the pancreatic head
response.rationale: All three are pancreatic cystic neoplasms, but IPMN is most common in the pancreatic head and can be large, while MCN typically favors body/tail and serous cystadenoma is rare and usually small. The location and size favor IPMN, though evidence is not highly specific.

rejected.why: Serous cystadenoma is rare and typically small, less consistent with an 11.8 cm head mass.
MCN more commonly occurs in the body/tail; head location is less typical, though not impossible.
